options.text: Carbon dioxide reacted with calcium hydroxide to form insoluble calcium carbonate.
The new white solid is calcium hydroxide.
Calcium carbonate makes lime water milky even when it is dissolved.
Bubbling the same gas into plain water also turns the water milky.

stem:
Vihaan mixes baking soda with vinegar. A gas forms. He bubbles the gas through clear lime water. Lime water is calcium hydroxide in water. The lime water turns milky.

Which claim correctly explains the milky appearance?

teacher.key_rationale: Carbon dioxide from the baking soda–vinegar mix reacts with lime water to form insoluble calcium carbonate, which makes the liquid look milky. The solid is not calcium hydroxide; dissolved carbonate would not cloud it the same way; plain water does not turn milky.
